public_rationale: Epoch AI's September 2026 methodology measures operationally available compute and explicitly excludes actual utilization rates [e1]. It therefore cannot establish full use or permanent non-use of the forecast's capacity cohort, or whether that use occurred without either stated customer exception [e1]. The supplied measurement leaves the conditional forecast unresolved [e1].
limitations: The capacity cohort is not enumerated, no deadline is stated, and 'virtually overnight' has no defined duration.
The packet lacks matched utilization and customer-spending records establishing whether both exceptions are absent.
Operational availability, reservations and announced contracts do not establish actual utilization.
Temporary vacancies cannot establish permanent non-use.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Not all of the AI compute being built will get used unless either Anthropic and OpenAI rent all of it or massive new customers (multiple $10 billion-a-year customers) appear virtually overnight.
conditions: unless Anthropic and OpenAI rent all of it
unless multiple $10 billion-a-year customers appear virtually overnight

statement.excerpt: The only way all that compute gets used is if either A) Anthropic and OpenAI rent all of it or B) massive (and I’m talking multiple $10 billion-a-year customers) appear virtually overnight.

from_speaker: The only way all that compute gets used
Anthropic and OpenAI rent all of it
our_interpretation: This is a necessary-condition forecast: without either stated exception, the capacity will not become fully used.
The capacity refers to the buildout discussed in the post, associated with roughly 30 GW and projected annual compute demand, not every existing AI chip.
No deadline is supplied. The nearby discussion of 2027 spending does not expressly set a utilization deadline.
Actual utilization must be distinguished from ownership, operational availability and reservation under a contract.
The spending threshold describes a condition on customer composition; the forecast's outcome measure is capacity utilization.
criteria.support_condition: For a clearly identified capacity cohort, both exceptions are absent and a decisive terminal event establishes that some capacity will never be used.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The identified capacity becomes fully used while neither lab rents all of it and no rapid emergence of multiple customers each spending at least $10 billion annually accounts for that use.

Obtain matched utilization and customer records showing either full use while both exceptions are absent, or a terminal event such as permanent retirement of unused capacity while both exceptions are absent.
